public_rationale: The original report establishes image-input capability and strong results across the named examinations. GRE writing is a material exception. The statement holds as a broad description, but would overstate the evidence if read as claiming exceptional performance on every subsection.
limitations: These were developer-run simulated examinations, not official candidate sittings.
The report discusses training-data contamination; the results are not wholly independent measurements.
Image capability did not imply general public availability.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: GPT-4 has vision capability and performs astonishingly well on standardized tests such as the LSAT, GRE, and SAT.

statement.excerpt: It can see (though we don’t have a lot of details on that yet); it does astonishingly well on a whole bunch of standardized tests, like LSATs, GREs, and SATs.

from_speaker: standardized tests, like LSATs, GREs, and SATs
our_interpretation: Seeing means accepting images and answering questions about their contents, without implying human-like visual understanding.
The ordinary reading of strong test performance is high standing relative to human test takers across the named examinations, not exceptional performance on every subsection.
The target is the original GPT-4 at publication. The launch-to-post interval is the latest publicly documented snapshot of this ongoing capability.
criteria.support_condition: Launch-model documentation establishes image understanding and high reported performance across the LSAT, GRE and SAT.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The launch model lacks image understanding, or comparable results show generally ordinary or poor performance across the named examinations.

evidence.excerpt:
This technical report presents GPT-4, a large multimodal model capable of processing image and
text inputs and producing text outputs.
evidence.locator: Section 1; examination results in Table 1; visual examples in Section 4 and Appendix G
evidence.explanation: The report documents launch-model image processing and reports approximately the 88th percentile on LSAT, 93rd on SAT reading/writing, 89th on SAT mathematics, 80th on GRE quantitative and 99th on GRE verbal. GRE writing was approximately the 54th percentile; event_date denotes the launch model's capability, not an asserted examination date.
